context: Reference natural implementation: a zero, one, or ambiguous lookup over a long list, testing whether the agent stops at the second match and branches on the three outcomes instead of collecting every match or taking the first one.

checklist.name: Creates RiderLookup.java
checklist.description: Creates RiderLookup.java with the riderByCode(InsurancePolicy, String) method, the CoverageRider and InsurancePolicy records, AmbiguousRiderException unchanged, the needed imports, and Java 17-compatible code that would compile.

checklist.name: Returns empty, the single match, or the domain exception
checklist.description: Matches with null-safe equality such as Objects.equals, returns Optional.empty() for no match, returns the one matching rider for a single match, and throws AmbiguousRiderException built from policy.policyNumber() and riderCode whenever two or more riders match. Score 0 if any path returns a rider while a second match exists, throws a different exception type, or throws on a null code.

checklist.name: Stops scanning at the second match
checklist.description: The work is bounded at two matches: filter(...).limit(2) before the terminal, or an equivalent that stops reading riders once a second match is seen. Score 0 for filter(...).toList(), collect(Collectors.toList()), count(), or grouping that reads every rider, and for a first lookup followed by a second full pass to check for duplicates.

checklist.name: Branches explicitly on zero, one, or ambiguous
checklist.description: A short stream pipeline produces at most two matches (filter, limit(2), toList or an equivalent collector), and a switch or if/else on the result size handles 0, 1, and more than 1 as separate visible branches. Score 12 for a correct bounded loop that remembers one match and throws on the second. Score 0 when the duplicate check hides inside a reduce or collector merge lambda that throws, or inside a multi-line lambda.

checklist.name: Does not settle the lookup by encounter order
checklist.description: Does not use findFirst() or findAny() as the selection step, since either one silently accepts duplicates. Score 0 if findFirst or findAny picks the result, even when a separate duplicate check is added after it.

checklist.name: Keeps the lookup focused
checklist.description: Adds no caches, indexes, dependencies, extra public types, or parallel streams, and the output contains no internal workflow labels such as hard stop, marker, scan, checklist, skill, rubric, or criteria.
